paper_summary.rationale: Cost-effective ($0.15/$0.6 per 1M tokens) with excellent quality for structured summaries. 128K context window handles full papers.

selection_summary.rationale: Fast and cost-effective for short inline summaries. Balances speed and quality.

qa.rationale: Excellent reasoning capabilities at low cost. Good for grounded Q&A with citations.

default.rationale: Default fallback model for any task type not explicitly configured.

paper_summary.rationale: Most cost-effective option ($0.25/$1.25 per 1M tokens). Fast with 200K context window. Excellent for high-volume summarization.

selection_summary.rationale: Ultra-fast and cheap for inline summaries. Perfect for quick context extraction.

qa.rationale: Best reasoning capabilities for complex Q&A. Higher cost but superior for understanding nuanced research questions.

paper_summary.rationale: Excellent for long documents with 1M token context. Cost-effective ($0.075/$0.3 per 1M tokens) for paper summarization.

selection_summary.rationale: Fast and very cheap. Ideal for quick inline summaries.

qa.rationale: Better reasoning for complex Q&A tasks. Higher quality responses for research questions.

paper_summary.rationale: Measured on the real 24kB full-paper payload: 6.2s / 4 findings, against gemma-4-26b:free at 47.1s / 3 findings. The free option was close enough to the request timeout to be the cause of /api/summarize aborting. ~5.7k tokens per summary is roughly $0.001 a paper.

selection_summary.rationale: Same model deliberately. The free nemotron-3-super was fine on short selections but returned an EMPTY findings array on full-paper input, and a model that fails silently by size is not one to keep on a hot path. Selection payloads are small, so the cost is a fraction of a cent.

qa.rationale: nemotron-3-ultra:free answers qa correctly but hit free-tier ResourceExhausted under load, which surfaces as an opaque 502. Paid flash removes that failure mode for about $0.001 a question. 1M context also covers the widest retrieval windows.

notes.selection_strategy: Models chosen based on cost-effectiveness and task-specific requirements. Summarization tasks prioritize cost while Q&A prioritizes reasoning quality.
notes.customization: Override specific models by setting environment variables: {PROVIDER}_{TASK}_MODEL (e.g., OPENAI_QA_MODEL=gpt-4o)
notes.openrouter_free_tier: OpenRouter rotates and retires :free slugs without notice — every model configured here before 2026-07-29 returned 404. If summarize or qa fail with a 404 naming a paid slug, re-check https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models for current :free ids rather than assuming a code fault.
notes.openrouter_model_selection: Pick on two measured properties, not on parameter count or blog rankings. (1) The model must honour response_format json_schema — this app calls generateJson everywhere. The catalogue's supported_parameters field is unreliable in BOTH directions: openai/gpt-oss-20b advertises structured_outputs and returns ```json-fenced markdown, while nemotron-3-ultra advertises neither and complies correctly. (2) It must still do the work on a realistic payload. nemotron-3-super passes a toy prompt but returns an empty findings array on a real 13.8kB paper. Always test with real chunk text. Payload size changes the winner: nemotron-3-ultra handles a 14kB excerpt in 8s but hits free-tier ResourceExhausted on a full 25kB paper, so paper_summary and qa deliberately use different models. Test at the size the task actually sends.
notes.openrouter_cost: The openrouter entries are intentionally PAID. Free slugs were tried first and are still the fallback (OPENROUTER_FALLBACK_MODELS=google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it:free): the free tier works but is 3-8x slower, rate-limits under load, and rotates without notice. deepseek-v4-flash costs about $0.001 per summary or question. Revisit if a free model matches it on the full-paper benchmark.
